note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Mary Smith, DOB 16-Aug-1976, presents with 2+ weeks of progressive left arm numbness, tingling and subjective weakness, worse since starting boxing classes.
- Urgent neurology referral arranged for further investigation (possible brain imaging); advised to attend A&E for any worsening neurological signs.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Left upper limb numbness, tingling, and weakness
- Timeline/progression: Symptoms present for at least two weeks, initially mild tingling progressing to numbness and subjective weakness.
- Distribution/associated symptoms: Numbness/tingling from elbow to hand; palmar (front) surface of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th digits affected; intermittent shoulder pain with movement; difficulty with fine motor tasks (piano); has dropped items/noticed decreased dexterity.
- Aggravating factors / history: Began after initiating a boxing class; tried massage and warm baths without improvement.
- Systems review / negatives: No leg weakness reported; walking normal; no seizures; sometimes has tired headaches; no regular visual disturbance at time of consult (see Issue 2).
- Examination findings: No formal documented physical exam or vitals in transcript; findings are patient-reported only.
- Differential considerations / specialist review: Treating clinician discussed possible entrapment/overuse injury related to boxing versus a neurological cause; clinician raised multiple sclerosis (MS) as a differential and arranged an urgent neurology referral.

Issue 2: Transient left-sided visual field loss
- Timeline/progression: Episode occurred a few weeks prior, lasted approximately 20 minutes and then resolved.
- Description/associated symptoms: Temporary loss of peripheral vision from the left eye; no associated ongoing visual symptoms at time of consult.
- Systems review / negatives: No persistent visual deficits reported; no reported vomiting or loss of consciousness associated with episode.
- Relevance: Clinician considered this episode concerning in the context of current sensory/motor symptoms and included in rationale for urgent neurology referral.

Issue 3: Recent viral illness / systemic symptoms
- Timeline/progression: Recent severe "cold/flu" approximately one month ago lasting about two weeks; patient reports fatigue since then.
- Association: Patient and clinician discussed possible temporal relationship between recent illness and current neurological symptoms.
- Social / activity impact: Fatigue has reduced exercise capacity; patient reports decreased activity on some days.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented (used intermittently for muscle/knuckle pain).
- Vitamin D — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Melatonin — dose/route/frequency not documented (occasional use for sleep).
- Iron supplements — recommended by GP but patient reports often forgets to take; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- None reported.

Past Medical History:
- Patient reports being generally healthy.
- Recent significant illness: severe cold/flu ~1 month ago lasting ~2 weeks.

Social History:
- Exercises regularly; attends a boxing class (started a few weeks ago).
- Plays piano.
- Social alcohol use; recent episode of heavier-than-usual drinking at a social event.
- Smoking status not documented.
- Living arrangements not documented.

Preventative History:
- No documentation of cervical screening, mammogram, prostate testing, fecal occult blood test, bone density, vaccinations, optometry review, or skin checks in the consult.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No clinician-recorded physical examination findings documented; neurological findings are patient-reported symptoms only.

Plan:
- Urgent neurology referral initiated for further assessment and likely brain imaging (clinician indicated a brain scan may be required).
- No medications started during this consult; clinician noted corticosteroids can be used for acute inflammatory causes (e.g., MS flare) but will only be considered after definitive diagnosis — steroids not prescribed at this visit.
- Safety/advice: Patient instructed to attend A&E promptly if weakness progresses to legs, vision worsens or persists, or if new severe headache, vomiting, or seizures occur.
- Follow-up: Await neurology appointment and imaging results; further management to be directed by neurology.

document_quality / Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: no documented vital signs; no formal neurological or physical examination recorded; medication dosages/routes/frequencies not provided; smoking status and quantified alcohol use not documented; exact dates for symptom onset and transient visual loss not precisely dated.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript: minor clarity issues — clinician briefly referred to a different name ("Edward"); transcript contains a brief unclear exchange regarding neck pain (patient and clinician statements overlap); otherwise no substantive clinical contradictions.
- Transcript quality comment: Audio/transcript largely coherent and intelligible with occasional interruptions and minor conversational fillers; clinical history extractable.
